newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt mostly higher, led by Bulgaria rally.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt mostly higher, led by Bulgaria rally.

text.p: Most emerging market debt prices climbed higher on Tuesday, particularly Bulgaria Brady's, which surged on news that general elections would be held by April 20, emerging market sources said.
After weeks of mass protests, Bulgaria's ruling Socialists assented to early elections.

That news sent Bulgaria IABs, FLRBs and discounts soaring more than two percentage points, traders said. The bonds rose further after the International Monetary Fund said it "welcomes the agreement" and hoped to resume loan talks.

"This is very similar to what you saw in Argentina before they began to stabilize, which is major political consensus building in the street," said Gary Evans, senior emerging market strategist at Lehman Brothers. "There were stories of protesters tearing down no-left-turn signs and carrying them through the streets."

At 1600 EST/2100 GMT, Bulgaria FLRBs BGFLIRB=RR were 3-1/2 firmer at 39 bid and its IABs BGFLTH11=RR were three percentage points higher at 52-1/8 bid. The country's discount bonds BGFLTH24A=RR were 2-1/8 stronger at 56 bid.
"We are, in some instances, 130 basis points tighter on discounts," one trader said. "It's kind of ridiculous."
Despite the tremendous surge in prices, Bulgaria debt remained relatively cheap, Evans said. "These levels are trading 600 to 700 basis points over comparably rated U.S. high-yield bonds," he said.
Traders said the bonds, generally quite illiquid, traded heavily during the New York session.

A widely supported, 48-hour general strike has been called for Wednesday to protest austerity measures and corruption in the government of President Abdala Bucaram. Analysts said the strike is yet another roadblock to convertibility.
The unrest prompted widespread selling, traders said.

"There's been a lot of negative press about the strike tomorrow and bonds have been under pressure for the last several days," one trader said. "That market has widened between 15 and 25 basis points."
Ecuador discounts ECDISC=RR slipped 1/2 to 69-5/8 bid, while the country's IEBs ECIEB=RR and PDIs ECPDI=RR both eased 1/4 to 87 bid and 62-7/8 bid respectively. Pars ECPARS=RR rose 1/4 to 46-1/4 bid.
William Romary, senior economist for Latin America at UBS Securities, said Ecuadorian unrest warranted investors' attention.
"The power and force of the strike will probably influence the president's ability to proceed with his reforms," Romary said.
More broadly, Brady bonds were mostly higher but yield spreads over U.S. Treasuries were mixed, with most coupons modestly wider, traders said.
At 1600 EST/2100 GMT, Argentina pars AR4C23=RR were 1/2 higher at 66-3/4 bid, Brazil "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were 5/8 firmer at 79-1/2 bid and Mexico discounts MXFLL19=RR were 1/8 better at 91-3/8 bid.
